text_blocks.snippet: A heart attack, also known as myocardial infarction, is primarily triggered by a blockage in one of the coronary arteries, which are the blood vessels that supply the heart muscle with oxygen-rich blood. This blockage usually occurs when a plaque (a buildup of cholesterol, fats, and other substances) ruptures and forms a blood clot that obstructs the artery.
snippet_highlighted_words: a blockage in one of the coronary arteries

list.snippet: CAD is the most common underlying cause of heart attacks.
Plaque buildup over time narrows the arteries, reducing blood flow.
This narrowing can lead to angina (chest pain) when the heart is stressed.

text_blocks.snippet: 2. Plaque Rupture and Blood Clot Formation:

list.snippet: A plaque buildup can rupture or tear, exposing the underlying tissue.
This triggers the formation of a blood clot at the site of the rupture, further blocking blood flow.
If the clot is large enough, it can completely block the artery, starving the heart muscle of oxygen.

list.title: Coronary Artery Spasm:
list.snippet: In some cases, a spasm or sudden contraction of the artery can also restrict blood flow, leading to a heart attack.

list.title: Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection (SCAD):
list.snippet: This is a rare condition where a tear occurs in the artery wall, causing a blockage.

list.title: Blood Clots from Other Parts of the Body:
list.snippet: In rare instances, a blood clot or air bubble from elsewhere in the body can travel to the coronary arteries and cause a blockage.
Age: Risk increases with age.
Family History: A family history of heart disease increases the risk.
Lifestyle Factors: Smoking, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, obesity, diabetes, and physical inactivity all contribute to the risk.
Other Conditions: Certain medical conditions like autoimmune diseases or infections can also increase the risk, according to the Cleveland Clinic.
Stress and Strong Emotions: Intense emotions like anger, grief, and even intense joy can trigger a heart attack in some individuals, according to WebMD.
A heart attack requires immediate medical attention to restore blood flow to the heart muscle and prevent permanent damage.
If the blockage isn't treated quickly, a part of the heart muscle can begin to die.

related_questions.question: Can you have a heart attack without knowing?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, it is possible to have a heart attack without realizing it. These are often referred to as silent heart attacks or silent myocardial infarctions. They can occur with minimal or no noticeable symptoms, or the symptoms can be easily mistaken for other less serious conditions like indigestion, muscle strain, or fatigue.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, it is possible to have a heart attack without realizing it

list.title: Subtle or absent symptoms:
list.snippet: Unlike classic heart attacks, silent heart attacks may not present with intense chest pain or other typical symptoms like shortness of breath, arm pain, or sweating.

list.title: Misinterpreted symptoms:
list.snippet: Symptoms like indigestion, fatigue, or muscle pain in the chest or back can be easily attributed to other causes, leading individuals to overlook the possibility of a heart attack.

text_blocks.snippet: What are the risks of silent heart attacks?

list.title: Delayed treatment:
list.snippet: Because the symptoms are not recognized as a heart attack, individuals may not seek timely medical attention, which can lead to more significant heart damage and increase the risk of complications or death.

list.title: Increased risk of future heart problems:
list.snippet: Even though they are called "silent," silent heart attacks still pose the same long-term risks as a heart attack with noticeable symptoms, including an increased risk of future heart attacks, heart failure, and other cardiovascular issues.

list.title: Mild or fleeting chest pain:
list.snippet: Instead of the intense, crushing chest pain associated with a classic heart attack, some may experience mild or intermittent chest discomfort, pressure, or a squeezing sensation.

list.title: Shortness of breath and/or dizziness:
list.snippet: These symptoms, often accompanied by a general feeling of illness or fatigue, can be mistaken for other conditions.

list.title: Indigestion:
list.snippet: Nausea, vomiting, or a feeling of indigestion, without any apparent digestive cause, can be an atypical sign of a silent heart attack.

list.title: Cold sweats, lightheadedness, or unexplained fatigue:
list.snippet: These symptoms, if persistent, should not be ignored.

list.title: Knowing the risk factors:
list.snippet: Understanding the risk factors for heart disease (high blood pressure, high cholesterol, smoking, diabetes, family history) is crucial for prevention and early detection.

list.title: Seeking medical attention:
list.snippet: If you experience any of the symptoms mentioned above, or if you have any concerns about your heart health, it's crucial to seek prompt medical attention. Early diagnosis and treatment are essential for minimizing heart damage and improving outcomes, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

text_blocks.snippet: A heart attack, also known as myocardial infarction, occurs when blood flow to the heart is suddenly blocked, depriving the heart muscle of oxygen and nutrients. This blockage is usually caused by a blood clot in a coronary artery, which is the vessel supplying blood to the heart. If the blockage isn't quickly resolved, the heart muscle tissue can be damaged or even die.
snippet_highlighted_words: occurs when blood flow to the heart is suddenly blocked, depriving the heart muscle of oxygen and nutrients

list.snippet: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD): The most common cause is the buildup of plaque (fatty deposits) in the coronary arteries, a condition called atherosclerosis. This plaque can rupture, leading to a blood clot that blocks the artery.
Blood Clot: Even without significant plaque buildup, a blood clot can form and block an artery.
Coronary Artery Spasm: In rare cases, a spasm of the coronary artery can restrict blood flow.
Chest Pain or Discomfort: This can feel like pressure, tightness, or squeezing in the chest.
Pain in Other Areas: The pain can radiate to the arms, jaw, neck, back, or stomach.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing can occur with or without chest pain.
Other Symptoms: Sweating, nausea, dizziness, lightheadedness, and fatigue are also common.
Call 911 immediately: A heart attack is a medical emergency.
Don't delay treatment: Prompt medical attention is crucial to minimize heart damage.
Be aware of the symptoms: Recognize the signs of a heart attack and seek help quickly.
